question: Romanian farmers with large farm holdings are unhappy at cereal crop prices, especially for wheat, on the local market. Global factors are making the socio-economic situation more complex, meaning that many farmers face financial difficulties, including the risk of bankruptcy. A growing number of farmers are forfeiting their farms as they are unable to pay their debts.
Experienced farmers consider that, in order for farmers to derive any real benefit, the price per kilogram of wheat should exceed RON 1 (EUR 0,20), when it currently stands at RON 0,95 (EUR 0,19).

Even that price offers little support for farmers, as production costs per hectare have increased significantly and cereal crops from Ukraine come at very low prices since fungicides, pesticides, insecticides, fertilisers and diesel cost much less than they do in the European Union.

Bearing these circumstances in mind, and in order to address these challenges, farmers need to seek support from government authorities and agricultural organisations. I would therefore like to ask the Commission whether it has given consideration to the difficulties being faced by these farmers and whether it is considering a plan to mitigate these difficulties?
answer: Global and EU cereal prices dropped significantly from their exceptional peaks of 2022 resulting, at that time, from the consequences of Russian aggression against Ukraine. This surge was only temporary, and prices are now back to a level observed in 2021. Romanian prices followed this general trend and continue evolving along their traditional pattern.

Input prices also dropped these last months, in particular for fertilisers which are now also back at a level closer to those of mid-2021. The Commission is closely following this aspect through its Fertilisers Market Observatory (1).

To address the difficulties of Romanian farmers affected by the increased imports of cereals and oilseeds from Ukraine, the Commission adopted in 2023 exceptional support measures of EUR 39.78 million and financed through the agricultural reserve. Since May 2023 Romanian imports of cereals from Ukraine practically stopped.

Cereals and oilseeds farmers can also benefit from support under the Romanian Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Plan 20232027, either in the form of direct payments or support for investments under rural development.

Regarding direct payments this includes decoupled support under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability, Complementary Redistributive Support for Sustainability and Complementary Income Support for Young Farmers. In addition, under eco-scheme, farmers may receive support for implementing environmentally friendly practices.

Important rural development support is also available to farmers for the acquisition of agricultural equipment in small farms, investments in conditioning, storage, and processing, modernisation and setting-up of irrigation infrastructure or for the payment of insurance premiums (2).
